note: A width-generic Verilog module toward VHDL, and the design that finds hif-backend#93. hif2vhdl encodes the parameter as a 32-bit signed generic with a bit-string literal default and rewrites every port bound as to_integer(W - "0000...0001"); vhdl2hif accepts it and hif2verilog then aborts in sortParameters with "Unable to get type of value". Hand-written VHDL spelling the same thing as `generic (W : integer := 5)` round-trips through those two tools cleanly, so the defect is hif2vhdl's encoding and not hif2verilog's handling. W is 5 rather than a power of two so a silently substituted width is a different number, and `top` reads a[W-1] so the parameter must reach the body and not only the port list. Distinct from parameterized/parameterized_width.v, a bare .v on plain_roundtrip that never simulates.
